newsitem.title: India: Indian troops hunt militants after Sunday massacre.
newsitem.headline: Indian troops hunt militants after Sunday massacre.

text.p: Soldiers in Indias northeastern state of Tripura shot dead a tribal separatist and captured five others when they tried to attack a village of Bengali settlers on Monday, officials said.

Troops with shoot-on-sight orders combed the areas of the states Khowai region, where at least 35 people died on Sunday and thousands were rendered homeless in an orgy of ethnic violence as tribals opposed to immigrants rampaged through three villages.
They shot dead people and set fire to houses in a fresh round of violence in the hilly tracts bordering Bangladesh.
Security forces posted in Khowai foiled an attack on a village and fired at the militants on Monday, officials said.
"One militant died on the spot and security forces captured five militants," said R.K. Bhaumik, a local police official.

Thousands of Bengali settlers have been rendered homeless and have taken shelter in relief camps. "There are eight refugee camps and over 15,000 people have taken shelter in these relief camps," said district official S.R. Deb.

"The situation is improving and the security forces are patrolling round-the-clock in sensitive areas of the Khowai sub-division," Lieutenant Colonel H.S. Brar, heading the security operations, told Reuters.

Tripuras indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy. Tribal militants have been pursuing a campaign seeking a separate tribal state for 17 years.
More than 2,000 people were killed in June 1980 in the regions worst ethnic riots.
On Sunday, three separatists died in clashes, police said, adding two others were shot dead by security forces policing an indefinite curfew in the Khowai area.
The separatists had set ablaze at least 100 homes in one village and fired on fleeing residents, police said in Agartala, the state capital.
It was the third attack in the Khowai area in a week. Tribal separatists had set fire to more than 60 houses in ethnic clashes the previous Sunday and killed 17 people on Monday.
Bengali refugees at the Chebri school, which has been converted into a relief shelter, shouted slogans against the state government.
"Not even a single minister of this government has visited the affected areas," said one refugee, Bulu Das.
The state government said the situation was calm but tense on Monday.
"The situation is under control and we are doing our best to normalise the situation. We appeal to the people to maintain peace," Tripuras Home (interior) Minister Samar Chowdhury said.

The states communist-led government came under attack from the opposition Congress party for the sharp surge in attacks over the past eight days by the separatist All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF), which has claimed 56 lives.
Local news agencies said Congress was pushing for the imposition of direct rule from New Delhi to stem the violence.
The Congress party shores up Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowdas United Front alliance in the federal parliament.
The Communist Party of India-Marxist, which heads a coalition governing Tripura and is part of the Left Front grouping, is a member of the United Front.
ATTF issued a statement last July telling Bengali settlers to leave the state, which has an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh.
